newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait approves U.S. troop deployment-official says.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait approves U.S. troop deployment-official says.

text.p: Kuwait on Monday approved a U.S. request to deploy additional ground troops in the Gulf Arab state amid heightened tension with Iraq, a Kuwaiti official said.
"Yes, we have agreed," the official, who declined to be identified, said by telephone. He said the deployment would be a little less than the 5,000 troops proposed by Washington.

The Clinton administration on Friday announced it had ordered 5,000 army troops from Fort Hood, Texas to join forces already in the Gulf in preparation for possible military action against Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry, on a visit to the Gulf to rally the Gulf War alliance against Saddam, on Sunday asked Kuwait's emir, Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah, for permission to proceed with the plan.

U.S. officials have said the Fort Hood troops -- members of two battalions and a Brigade Combat Team headquarters as well as backup maintenance and medical staff -- would be deployed under Exercise Intrinsic Action, a programme begun last year to train Kuwaiti soldiers.
